The test image shows corn plants with prominent pale/white linear streaks running parallel to leaf veins across multiple leaves. This is characteristic of a viral disease. Key observations:
- Whole plant affected
- Narrow pale-yellowish/white streaks running lengthwise along leaves
- No discrete lesions or spots
- Plants appear somewhat stunted

Top candidates: Maize_streak_virus, Maize_dwarf_mosaic_virus, Corn_Stunt_Spiroplasma

The Maize_streak_virus reference images match very well — showing the same narrow pale/white streaks running parallel to leaf veins, with the field view (top-right of reference collage) nearly identical to the test image. Corn_Stunt_Spiroplasma shows reddish/purple discoloration — very different. Maize_dwarf_mosaic_virus shows broader mosaic/stripe patterns.

All comparisons confirm the diagnosis:

- **Maize_streak_virus**: Reference collage (especially top-right panel) is nearly identical to the test image — same narrow pale/white streaks parallel to veins on full-grown plants, same field appearance
- **Maize_chlorotic_dwarf_virus**: Different pattern — more general yellowing/chlorosis, not narrow streaks
- **Stewarts_wilt**: Young seedlings, pale/dying plants — very different
- **Goss_wilt**: Brown/necrotic lesions on leaves — very different

The test image shows classic **Maize streak virus** — narrow, pale-yellow/white streaks running strictly parallel to leaf veins across entire plants, characteristic of leafhopper-transmitted MSV, common in sub-Saharan Africa.
